\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{मोल} (mol)}{मोल (mol)}]{\mw{मोल} (mol) — the cost; worth}

\label{lesson:MW-C213-mol}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for double, then the Marwadi for a chhatak.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{मोल}}
\textbf{\mw{मोल}} — \emph{mol} — \textquotedblleft{}the cost; worth\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{मोल} \mw{पूछो}, \mw{पछै} \mw{खरीदो।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mol pūchho, pachhai kharīdo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Ask the cost, then buy.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{मोल}} (\emph{mol}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{maulya}, \textquotedblleft{}price\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{mola}, \textquotedblleft{}price\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10373).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mol}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mol}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mol pūchho, pachhai kharīdo.} — Ask the cost, then buy.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for double, then the Marwadi for a chhatak, then say \emph{mol} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{घटणो} (ghaṭṇo)}{घटणो (ghaṭṇo)}]{\mw{घटणो} (ghaṭṇo) — to decrease; to come down}

\label{lesson:MW-C213-ghatno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a chhatak, then the Marwadi for the cost.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{घटणो}}
\textbf{\mw{घटणो}} — \emph{ghaṭṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to decrease; to come down\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{आजकाल} \mw{भाव} \mw{घटै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ājkāl bhāv ghaṭai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Prices are coming down these days.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \mw{वो} \mw{भाव} \mw{घट्यो}, \emph{vo bhāv ghaṭyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{घटणो}} (\emph{ghaṭṇo}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*ghaṭṭati}, \textquotedblleft{}decreases\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists the Old Marwari verb \emph{ghaṭai}, \textquotedblleft{}decreases\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4415).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghaṭṇo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghaṭṇo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ājkāl bhāv ghaṭai hai.} — Prices are coming down these days.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for a chhatak, then the Marwadi for the cost, then say \emph{ghaṭṇo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{घटणो} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To decrease; to come down\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{घटावणो} (ghaṭāvṇo)}{घटावणो (ghaṭāvṇo)}]{\mw{घटावणो} (ghaṭāvṇo) — to lower (a price)}

\label{lesson:MW-C213-ghatavno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for the cost, then the Marwadi for to decrease.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{घटावणो}}
\textbf{\mw{घटावणो}} — \emph{ghaṭāvṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to lower (a price)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{आप} \mw{भाव} \mw{थोड़ु} \mw{घटावो।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āp bhāv thoṛu ghaṭāvo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Please lower the price a little.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \mw{म्हैं} \mw{भाव} \mw{घटायो}, \emph{mhaĩ bhāv ghaṭāyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{घटावणो}} (\emph{ghaṭāvṇo}) is the causative of \textbf{\mw{घटणो}}, \textquotedblleft{}to decrease\textquotedblright{}, inherited from the same reconstructed \emph{*ghaṭṭati}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{ghaṭāvai}, which it glosses \textquotedblleft{}belittles\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4415).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{मुफत} (muphat)}{मुफत (muphat)}]{\mw{मुफत} (muphat) — free of charge}

\label{lesson:MW-C213-muphat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to decrease, then the Marwadi for to lower.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{मुफत}}
\textbf{\mw{मुफत}} — \emph{muphat} — \textquotedblleft{}free of charge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{अठै} \mw{पाणी} \mw{मुफत} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aṭhai pāṇī muphat hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Water is free here.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{मुफत}} (\emph{muphat}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{muft}, \textquotedblleft{}free, gratis\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{बिकणो} (bikṇo)}{बिकणो (bikṇo)}]{\mw{बिकणो} (bikṇo) — to be sold; to sell}

\label{lesson:MW-C213-bikno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to lower, then the Marwadi for free of charge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{बिकणो}}
\textbf{\mw{बिकणो}} — \emph{bikṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to be sold; to sell\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{ये} \mw{घी} \mw{जल्दी} \mw{बिकै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ye ghī jaldī bikai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This ghee sells quickly.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \mw{वो} \mw{घी} \mw{बिक्यो}, \emph{vo ghī bikyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{बिकणो}} (\emph{bikṇo}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{vikrīyate}, \textquotedblleft{}is sold\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry, but lists Hindi \emph{biknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be sold\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11642).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}
